item.content:encoded:
The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ Zac Affleck shared a sweet birthday tribute to daughter Nora, 5, hours after news broke that wife Jen Affleck had filed for divorce.
“Happy Birthday to my baby girl! You have the biggest heart and make everything feel a little extra magical. I love you,” Zac, 30, captioned a video montage of moments with his daughter posted via Instagram on Wednesday, November 4.
Zac and Jen, 27, also share son Luca, 3, and daughter Penny, 16 months. Jen is currently pregnant with the estranged couple’s fourth child.
TMZ reported on Wednesday that Jen had filed for divorce from Zac in Utah on Tuesday, November 3, one day before Nora’s birthday. The reality star submitted a proposed parenting plan, though the details of the document remain private.
Jen and Zac rose to fame in 2024 on Hulu’s The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives. Jen is also set to appear on spinoff The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, which premieres on November 12.
The Mormon couple announced that they were expecting baby No. 4 in June. A month later, Jen opened up about once again experiencing prenatal depression.
“Prenatal depression came back this pregnancy. Only this time, it came back even heavier,” Jen wrote via Instagram on July 23. “There were many days during my first trimester where my mind went to some really dark places. It scared me. And if you’ve ever experienced depression, you know how isolating it can feel. Add moving to a new state, being pregnant, and trying to show up for your kids, and some days felt impossible.”
“Friends, family, strangers… people who had no idea how much they were carrying me just by being there,” she wrote. “They reminded me that even when I couldn’t see the light, I wasn’t walking through the darkness alone.”
She continued, “I don’t believe depression is beautiful. It’s painful, confusing, and exhausting. But I do believe God can bring beauty from it. It has made me ask deeper questions. It has made me slow down. It has reminded me what really matters. It has taught me that strength sometimes looks like asking for help instead of pretending you’re OK.”
In April 2025, Jen opened up about her marriage to Zac in an exclusive interview with Us while promoting the second season of Mormon Wives.
“[Our marriage is] night and day difference at this point,” she said at the time. “Every single day we tell each other. We’re like, if we can get through this, we can get through anything.”

item.content:encoded:
After 14 years of marriage, Hila Klein has finally filed for divorce from Ethan Klein amid rumours that he was involved in an extramarital affair that lasted for more than six months. In the filing, it shows that Hila filed for divorce on November 2, 2026, with October 13 as the date of separation. The divorce petition includes her request for joint custody of their three boys, spousal support, and reimbursement for her legal fees.
Hila and Ethan got married on October 10, 2012. They have three kids together: Theodore, who is seven years old, Bruce, who is four years old, and Sunny, who is two years old. In the divorce document, Hila Klein asked for joint custody of all three kids. She is also seeking financial support from Ethan and wants him to cover her attorney's fees.
Their divorce news came within two weeks following Hila's October 22 Instagram statement, where she detailed how she uncovered the alleged affair of Ethan's. Ethan told her it was a mere kiss to begin with, but he later referred to it as emotional cheating before allegedly confirming the affair, which spanned over six months.
“The betrayal I feel is immeasurable,” Hila wrote in her statement. She said that she has trusted Ethan for 20 years as a husband, father of their kids, and business partner. She also mentioned that she did not yet know all about the claimed affair. Her priority, she said, was taking care of herself and their children while navigating separation and co-parenting.
The divorce also took a toll on the couple's professional career. The H3 Podcast declared an indefinite hiatus before these allegations came to light. This production company confirmed that it would no longer produce content involving Ethan. Expressing support for Hila, the crew stated, “We stand with Hila and will support her every step of the way.”

item.content:encoded:
Frankie Muniz isn’t racing away from his struggles.
The Malcolm in the Middle actor got candid about what he’s been going through over the last six weeks, admitting his life has felt like “a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from.”
“Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time,” Muniz posted on X Sept. 18. “I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone.”
The admission comes over two months after he and wife Paige Price—with whom he shares 5-year-old son Mauz Mosley Muniz—announced their divorce after six years of marriage.
Still, there is a silver lining for the 40-year-old, as he explained, “The unexpected gift in the middle of it is that I’ve had nowhere to hide. I’ve had time to sit with myself, do real self-reflection, and finally see the areas of my life that need work if I want to become a better version of me. Not the polished version I show the world...the actual one.”
Muniz said he recently read that "sometimes hitting rock bottom is the thing that wakes you up" and becomes a catalyst to force “the changes you needed to make all along so you can live the best life possible.”
And that idea stayed with the race car driver, who imagined in five years time he will “look back at this exact low point and feel grateful for it,” especially because getting to a better place in his life necessitated going through the difficulty.
“This isn’t the end of the story. It’s the part where I start doing the work...the uncomfortable, unglamorous, necessary work. I’m choosing to treat this season as the foundation, not the finish line,” Muniz wrote. “If you’re in a low place right now too, you’re not broken. You’re being rebuilt. Let's keep going!”
In recent weeks, Muniz has been open about the difficult time he’s been facing, posting on X Aug. 26, “Am I naive to say that I didn't know that having a broken heart actually meant your heart physically aches. I'd rather break my back again.”
On Sept. 1 he wrote, “Struggling,” and a few days later on Sept. 6 shared two photos of himself as a child, captioning the pictures, “Sometimes I wish I could go back to this.”
